findings.name: Set Up Customer Engagement
findings.detail: To set up Customer Engagement for Life Sciences, install the Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement managed package in your org, set up the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app, and configure Customer Engagement features for use on web and mobile platforms. We've grouped features in alphabetical order within feature groups such as Account Management, Engagement Planning, and Engagement Execution. Learn About Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Unify and elevate every step of your commercial engagement strategy with Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement. With this add-on to Agentforce Life Sciences, your pharma or medtech organization can engage healthcare professionals with compliant, AI-powered tools for visits, content delivery, and strategic account planning. Set Up Customer Engagement with AI Skills Automate the multi-step Customer Engagement setup process using AI coding agents. Plan Your Customer Engagement Implementation Learn how to gather business requirements, sequence feature deployment, set project milestones, import data, and work with your business users to implement Customer Engagement successfully. Build Your Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Solution For a successful rollout, it’s crucial to understand the implementation sequence for Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement. We recommend you take a phased approach to implementation. A phased approach helps you strategically determine the order in which you configure and deploy Customer Engagement features, especially when many of these features have interdependencies.A phased approach helps you build a solid foundation, avoid compliance issues, and accelerate your time to value. Supported Platform Features and Components in Agentforce Life Sciences Learn which automation features the Agentforce Life Sciences desktop (Lightning web) experience supports and which automation features the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports. Also, learn which Salesforce Platform features, Lightning templates, and standard Lightning page components the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports. Get Your Org Ready for Customer Engagement Complete tasks that impact your entire org before you install the Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement managed package. After you install the managed package, complete more tasks that impact your entire org. Set Up the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile App Set up the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app to enable your field users to securely connect with healthcare professionals and organizations through their iPads. Field users can access and work with critical data, content (PDFs, HTML5, videos), reports, and smart summaries with or without an internet connection. Set Up the Life Sciences Customer Engagement Home Page The home page in Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement provides a centralized view of critical information and tasks so your users can prioritize their work. Customize the home page to show announcements, upcoming activities, visits to submit, prioritized accounts, and more. To show each user what matters most to them, tailor the home page for different profiles. Set Up Account Management Features Manage your relationships with healthcare organizations (HCOs) and healthcare professionals (HCPs). Gain a comprehensive view of HCPs and HCOs, including their contact and social network details, specialties, affiliations, business licenses, ratings, as well as territory and product, and team-specific details. Set Up Engagement Planning Features Optimize daily schedules, prioritize key events, and manage routines with Calendar. Log and manage time away from your territory with Time Off Territory. Improve your plans’ chances of success with reusable goal definition templates. Personalize action plan templates for Key Account Management. Identify growth opportunities and adapt to evolving customer needs with Account Plans. Drive initiatives targeted at key accounts in a region with Territory Business Plans. Set Up Engagement Execution Features Streamline scheduling, pre-visit planning, in-visit execution, and post-visit reporting processes with Visit Management. Capture, manage, and honor consent and communication preferences of healthcare professionals with Consent Management. Use Remote Engagement to host virtual meetings with customers. Use Medical Inquiries to deliver fast, compliant, and trusted responses to every HCP inquiry. Use Surveys to collect feedback from customers. Set Up Intelligent Content Features Equip field teams with a comprehensive content library so they can deliver impactful presentations and monitor engagement. Enable personalized communications with healthcare professionals and organizations by providing your field team with preapproved, customizable email templates. Set Up Order Management Features Run structured store checks and capture quoted orders, with pricing, discounts, and approvals, for pharmacy and provider visits. Set Up Product Management Features In the Life Sciences industry, delivering value to customers—healthcare professionals, organizations, and patients—depends on making sure that the right products are available, accessible, and aligned with regulatory requirements. In Agentforce Life Sciences, Product Management supports this goal by making it easier to configure, classify, and manage the products that your organization discusses, markets, sells, and distributes. Set Up Sample Management Features Enable pharmaceutical companies to efficiently handle and distribute drug samples to healthcare providers. Enhance drug sales and keep healthcare providers informed about the safe and effective use of products, leading to quicker treatments. Track and manage sales representative inventories of samples, ensuring compliance with regulations, and maintaining accurate records of distribution. Effective sample management is crucial for supporting healthcare providers and low-income patients, and ensuring ethical practices and regulatory compliance. Set Up Event Management Features Minimize administrative workload, support regulatory governance, and ensure the consistent and compliant execution of field events with Event Management. Set Up Common Customer Engagement Components Notify users of critical updates with App Alerts. Prevent legal and regulatory violations by making informed decisions with License Validation Checks. Manage complex business processes and guide users through their tasks with clear steps with multi-step workflows and related lists. Maximize customer engagement efficiency with Multi-Object Components and Dynamic Tree Views. Create Quick and Custom Actions for smoother workflows. Visualize Sales Data for effective customer interactions. Integrate Data 360 and Tableau Next with Customer Engagement Integrate Data 360 and Tableau Next with Life Sciences to transform complex life sciences data into actionable insights and enhanced visualizations. Tableau Next requires Data 360 and the Data 360 semantic layer. Set up Sales Data reports to help your users better understand their customers and plan effective interactions. Use Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Features Perform Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement tasks such as managing HCO and HCP accounts, planning and executing engagements with your customers, managing key accounts, and managing samples. Leverage Customer Engagement Best Practices Leveraging extensive past experience in CRM, Medtech, and Life Sciences implementations, Salesforce has compiled best practices from partners, clients, and professional services. These insights, gathered over eight years from common mistakes and configuration issues, aim to guide future implementations for clients, partners, and professional services. Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Patch Releases We release patches periodically. The patch updates in this section provide information on each patch release for the Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement package and Life Sciences Cloud mobile app.

findings.name: What Is Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement?
findings.detail: Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement is a native Salesforce application that helps commercial and medical field teams to plan, execute, and track healthcare organization (HCO) and healthcare professional (HCP) engagement across all channels, such as in-person visits, virtual meetings, email, and digital touchpoints. Built on the Salesforce Platform, it combines enterprise security with life sciences-specific capabilities such as sample management, compliant content delivery, and medical inquiry tracking. Your field teams can use the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app to securely connect with healthcare professionals through an agent-first, deeply unified, consumer grade mobile experience designed for the modern life sciences industry. Use the app’s offline capabilities to access and work with critical data, content, reports, and smart summaries, with or without an internet connection. findings.name: Medical Science Liaisons
findings.detail: Medical Science Liaisons (MSLs) conduct scientific engagement with healthcare providers on clinical topics while maintaining compliance boundaries. What MSLs Do Share medical resources such as publications and clinical trial data materials Respond to unsolicited medical information requests Document and analyze medical insights for medical affairs reporting Assess adverse event information for pharmacovigilance Collaborate with commercial teams within appropriate separation guidelines

findings.name: Field Managers
findings.detail: Field managers oversee territory performance, coach field teams, and monitor execution of activity plans. findings.detail: Data 360 creates unified HCP and HCO profiles by connecting internal systems, third-party data providers, and unstructured content, all of which powers AI insights and personalized engagement. What You Can Do with Data 360 Enrich HCP profiles with external prescribing data and affiliations Unify engagement history across commercial and medical teams Power Agentforce recommendations with complete account context Analyze unstructured content (documents, audio transcripts, videos) Query data in place that use zero-copy architecture How Field Teams Use Data 360 ROLE | EXAMPLE Sales Representatives | Access enriched HCP profiles with prescribing patterns and publication history Key Account Managers | View multi-stakeholder relationships across complex institutional accounts Medical Science Liaisons | Conduct scientific engagement and respond to medical information requests Field Managers | Identify HCPs' research interests, clinical trial participation, and congress activity Commercial Operations | Analyze territory performance with real-time activity and goal tracking Zero-Copy Architecture Data 360 queries data where it lives rather than copying it into Salesforce. findings.detail: Learn how to gather business requirements, sequence feature deployment, set project milestones, import data, and work with your business users to implement Customer Engagement successfully.

findings.name: Gather Requirements
findings.detail: Effective discovery and requirements gathering are paramount for a successful Life Sciences for Customer Engagement implementation. This phase helps your organization to lay the foundational understanding of your current state, future state, and the critical processes that drive your business. This phase isn't merely about collecting a list of "wants," but rather a deep dive into "why" those wants exist. It’s a collaborative effort between the implementation team and key stakeholders from various departments, including sales, marketing, legal, medical, finance, operations, and IT. As part of this analysis, focus on identifying pain points, inefficiencies, and opportunities for automation and improvement. Depending on your business, use all Life Sciences for Customer Engagement features or only some of them. As part of your planning, identify which features are necessary to fulfill your organizational goals. Many companies find success by implementing in stages, gradually building up to a fully realized Life Sciences solution. Here are key questions for your organization to answer, grouped by the following topics.

findings.name: Customer Data and Segmentation Questions
findings.detail: How do you currently maintain and verify healthcare professional (HCP) and healthcare organization (HCO) data such as National Provider Identifiers (NPIs), affiliations, and specialties? What data sources do you use (internal, third-party, claims, prescriber data)? How do you segment customers for engagement strategies (prescribing behavior, influence, specialties)? How do you identify and tier key opinion leaders, early adopters, and high-value accounts? What processes exist for data stewardship and maintaining customer hierarchies (HCO relationships)? How do you track customer preferences, interests, and therapeutic area focus? What consent management processes are in place for different engagement channels?

findings.name: Omni-Channel Engagement and Orchestration Questions
findings.detail: What channels do you currently use to engage customers (face-to-face, remote, email, web, events)? How do you coordinate engagement across multiple brands and therapeutic areas? How do you determine the right channel mix for different customer segments? What processes exist for triggered or event-based engagement (new prescriptions, formulary changes)? How do you manage engagement frequency and prevent over-saturation? How do you personalize content and messaging based on customer insights? What measurement exists for channel effectiveness and customer response?

findings.name: Field Team Planning and Execution Questions
findings.detail: How are territories designed and aligned (geography, accounts, therapeutic area)? What is the current process for activity planning (cycle planning)? How do field teams prioritize which customers to engage and when? What tools and processes support pre-call planning and research? How do you manage goals and objectives at the territory and individual rep level? What coordination is needed between different field roles (sales, MSL, patient support)? How do you handle territory changes, account reassignments, and coverage gaps?

findings.name: Visit and Interaction Management Questions
findings.detail: How do field teams currently schedule and conduct customer visits? What information needs to be captured during interactions (discussion topics, customer needs, objections)? How do you track promotional vs. non-promotional (medical/scientific) interactions? What approval processes exist for interaction documentation and compliance review? What do you capture attendees at group presentations? What mobile capabilities are required for field teams (offline access, real-time updates)? How do you manage joint visits and cross-functional collaboration?

findings.name: Content and Resource Management Questions
findings.detail: What types of content do teams use during engagements (detail aids, studies, patient resources)? How is promotional content approved and kept current? How do you track which content is used with which customers? What processes exist for medical/legal/regulatory (MLR) review and expiration management? How do you measure content effectiveness and customer engagement with materials? What customization or personalization is needed for different customer types? How do you distribute updates and new resources to field teams?

findings.name: Sample and Product Distribution Questions
findings.detail: What products require physical samples vs. shipped? How are samples allocated and distributed to field teams? What tracking is required for sample transactions (batch numbers, expiration, attestation)? How do you manage sample inventory and reconciliation? What processes exist for handling recalls, returns, or expired products? How do you ensure compliance with sample accountability regulations? What signature capture and documentation is required?

findings.name: Medical Affairs and Scientific Exchange Questions
findings.detail: How do medical science liaisons (MSLs) currently plan and document scientific exchanges with HCPs? What processes differentiate medical information requests from promotional interactions? How do you track unsolicited requests and off-label discussions? What coordination exists between MSLs and commercial teams (without inappropriate influence)? How do you manage publication planning and investigator-initiated studies? What processes exist for adverse event reporting from medical interactions? How do you measure medical affairs impact and stakeholder relationships?

findings.name: Analytics and Insights Questions
findings.detail: What metrics do you currently track for engagement effectiveness? How do you measure customer sentiment, satisfaction, and relationship strength? What data do you use to understand prescribing behavior and market trends? How do you attribute commercial activities to business outcomes? What dashboards or reporting do field teams and leadership need? How do you generate next-best-action recommendations for field teams? What predictive analytics or AI capabilities would enhance engagement strategies?

findings.name: Compliance and Quality Questions
findings.detail: What regulatory requirements govern customer interactions in your markets? How do you ensure field team adherence to promotional guidelines? What processes exist for monitoring and auditing field activities? How do you manage adverse event detection and reporting workflows? What training and certification tracking is required for field roles? How do you handle spend transparency and aggregate spend tracking (Sunshine Act, etc.)? What processes exist for handling customer complaints or product quality issues?

findings.name: Integration and Technology Ecosystem Questions
findings.detail: What systems currently support customer engagement (CRM, data vendors, marketing automation)? What integrations are critical for seamless workflows? How do you manage foundational data across systems (HCP/HCO golden records)? What legacy systems need to be retired, integrated, or replaced? What are your requirements for mobile, cloud, and offline capabilities? How do you ensure data security and access controls across systems? What reporting and Business Intelligence (BI) tools are used for analytics?

findings.name: Plan Timeline & Implementation Scope
findings.detail: Think about major rollout milestones and start plotting a timeline. Try to schedule implementation activities when your team can work without distractions. Avoid things like a major product launch, annual conference, or extended travel. The project’s timeline can expand or contract due to factors like: The scope of features and functionality your organization plans to implement. The level of feature customization needed. Online customer or partner portals. The effort required to extract, transform, and import your existing master and transactional data. Integration requirements with external data systems. The availability of subject matter experts, key stakeholders, and user acceptance testers. The experience of the project team with Salesforce technologies. The project’s budget allocation.

findings.name: Build Your Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Solution
findings.detail: For a successful rollout, it’s crucial to understand the implementation sequence for Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement. We recommend you take a phased approach to implementation. A phased approach helps you strategically determine the order in which you configure and deploy Customer Engagement features, especially when many of these features have interdependencies.A phased approach helps you build a solid foundation, avoid compliance issues, and accelerate your time to value. While every organization’s journey is unique, most Life Sciences Clouds for Customer Engagement implementations follow a logical progression.

findings.name: Phase 1: Foundation - Customer Data & Integrations
findings.detail: Establish your customer data, which is the foundation of your Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement solution. Nearly all subsequent features depend on having accurate, compliant HCP and HCO data properly structured and segmented. Key Activities: Design integration architecture with MDM, data vendors, and core systems Configure HCP/HCO data model and hierarchies (affiliations, referral networks) Integrate third-party data sources (NPIs, prescriber data, specialties) Set up customer segmentation and targeting strategies Establish consent management framework Define data governance and stewardship processes Establish customer master data quality processes Configure sample management system integration

findings.name: Phase 2: Essential Engagement - Field Planning & Execution
findings.detail: Enable your field teams to engage customers effectively. Configure territory alignment, activity planning, and basic visit management workflows so teams can begin structured customer interactions. Key Activities: Design and assign territories (geography, accounts, affiliations) Define product hierarchies and assign to territories Configure call planning and activity management Set up goal management and KPIs by territory/role Implement basic visit documentation workflows Enable mobile capabilities for field access

findings.name: Phase 3: Content & Compliance
findings.detail: Ensure compliant engagement. Before scaling engagement activities, establish approved content delivery and compliance guardrails. Key Activities: Set up MLR-approved content delivery Integrate MLR review and approval workflows outcomes Implement sample management and accountability tracking Configure adverse event detection and reporting Establish promotional vs. non-promotional interaction boundaries

findings.name: Phase 4: Advanced Engagement
findings.detail: From this point, your implementation journey becomes more tailored, depending on which additional Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement capabilities align with your business goals and current priorities. For example, you might then set up: Omnichannel Orchestration: For coordinating engagement across multiple channels (email, events, remote, digital) with unified customer journeys and intelligent next-best-actions. Medical Affairs Integration: To enable scientific exchange workflows for MSLs while maintaining appropriate separation from commercial activities.

findings.name: Phase 5: Intelligence & Optimization
findings.detail: Analytics & Insights: To gain deeper understanding of engagement effectiveness, customer sentiment, prescribing patterns, and commercial ROI. AI-Powered Recommendations: To enable predictive next-best-actions, intelligent territory recommendations, and personalized engagement strategies. Omnichannel Attribution: To understand cross-channel impact and optimize engagement mix by customer segment.

findings.name: Phase 6: Advanced Compliance & Quality
findings.detail: Advanced Monitoring & Quality Assurance: Enhanced audit trails, real-time compliance alerts, and quality scoring for field interactions. Aggregate Spend Tracking: Automated transparency reporting (Sunshine Act, EFPIA) with transfer of value calculations if you are using Visit Expenses. Pharmacovigilance Integration: Advanced adverse event workflows with case management and regulatory submission capabilities.

findings.name: Critical Success Factors
findings.detail: Start with Data Quality: Without clean, accurate HCP/HCO data, all downstream engagement will suffer. Invest time in Phase 1. Compliance is Not Optional: Don’t rush past Phase 3. Regulatory violations can have severe consequences in Life Sciences. Change Management is Key: Field teams need training, adoption support, and clear value demonstration at each phase. Measure & Iterate: Build measurement into each phase so you can demonstrate value and refine your approach before scaling. Think Omnichannel from Day One: Even if you start with field visits, design your data model and processes to accommodate future channels.

findings.name: Get Your Org Ready for the Customer Engagement Managed Package
findings.detail: Complete tasks before you install the Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement managed package in your org. The package installation process fails when you don’t complete these prerequisite tasks.

findings.name: Required Editions

User Permissions Needed To complete package pre-installation: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin and Health Cloud Starter permission sets Warning Make sure to install the Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement managed package in a new, blank org that doesn't contain pre-existing configurations. Confirm with your Account Executive during license provisioning that the licenses are applied to a new, blank org. If you plan to install the managed package in an org with pre-existing configurations, evaluate the org to test the potential impact.

findings.name: Assign Permission Sets to Your Admin User Account
findings.detail: Assign the Life Sciences Commercial Admin and Health Cloud Starter permission sets to your admin user account. These permission sets provide access to Customer Engagement features, data model objects, and metadata objects. From Setup, use the Quick Find box to search for and select Users , and then select your admin user account. Scroll to Permission Set Assignments, and then click Edit Assignments . Move Health Cloud Starter and Life Sciences Commercial Admin to the Enabled Permission Sets list from the Available Permission Sets list, and then save your changes. Scroll to Permission Set License Assignments and verify that Health Cloud Starter and Life Sciences Commercial are listed. These licenses are automatically added when you assign the permission sets.

findings.name: Configure Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup Settings
findings.detail: Configure settings from the Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup page. Turn on Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup. This setting activates foundational Customer Engagement features in your org and unlocks additional setup settings. From Setup, use the Quick Find box to search for and select Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup . Turn on Life Sciences Customer Engagement . The Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup page shows more settings. Turn on RSVP Email Address to create the email address that receives and handles responses from iCalendar invitations. This is a prerequisite setting for email administration in Life Sciences Customer Engagement. To learn more, see Get Your Org Ready for Emails . Turn on Surveys and configure survey settings. Customer Engagement uses Survey Invitation and Survey Subject objects for tracking customer feedback. These objects become available when you turn on Surveys. Expand the Get Your Org Ready to Use Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement section, then click Configure Surveys . From the Surveys page, turn on Surveys . You can now access the Survey Invitation and Survey Subject objects in Object Manager. Turn on Survey Owners Can Manage Responses . Leave the other settings blank, and return to the Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup page. Note Configure territories later in this topic. Turn on settings for package installation. These settings enable Salesforce features that the package depends on. The package installation fails without them. From the Get Your Org Ready to Use Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement section, click Verify and Enable Settings to show the list of settings. Click Enable All . Click Close after all settings are turned on. Warning Don't turn off any of these prerequisite settings or feature preferences via metadata APIs. Doing so causes future upgrades of the package to fail. Configure organization-wide default sharing settings. The package requires specific sharing defaults to function properly and maintain data security. From the Get Your Org Ready to Use Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement section, click Configure Sharing . Click Edit . Verify the default internal and external access for the Account and Contract object is Private . If it isn’t, update the access, and acknowledge the UI messages that appear. Verify the default internal and external access for the Case and Opportunity objects is Private . If it isn’t, update the access. For the Provider Affiliation and Provider Affiliation Product objects, change the default internal access to Public Read/Write . To enable the automatic sharing of Contact Point Best Contact Time records, turn on Best Contact Time Custom Sharing . To enable the automatic sharing of Contact Point Social records, turn on Contact Point Social Custom Sharing . To enable the automatic sharing of Provider Account Territory Summary records, turn on Territory-Based Derived Sharing . To align the products associated with a territory with the territory's parents, turn on Parent Territory Product Alignment . To filter the product hierarchy view by the current user's business group, turn on Product Hierarchy Business Group Filter . To automatically share subject assignments based on the associated managed event's sharing settings, turn on Event-Based Derived Sharing for Subject Assignment . findings.name: Set Up Customer Engagement with Salesforce Go Solution
findings.detail: Salesforce Go provides a seamless, automated configuration process to accelerate your Customer Engagement setup. Instead of navigating through disparate manual steps, you can install the metadata, enable core features, and deploy sample data from a single interface.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Prerequisite
findings.detail: Before you set up Customer Engagement using Salesforce Go, install the Customer Engagement managed package . On the Agentforce Life Sciences Customer Engagement Setup page, you can choose between setup options that are tailored to your organizational needs. Regardless of the path you choose, the setup bundles automate the heavy lifting of your Customer Engagement setup. Standard Installation: A one-click process that installs everything required to get started, including metadata, configurations, profiles, page layouts, and sample data. Custom Installation: Provides the flexibility to preserve existing configurations or install components specific to your organizational needs. You can choose between the Core Configuration and Enhanced Experience optional bundles. The Custom Profile bundle is mandatory. Custom Profile Bundle: Deploys the LSC Custom Profile that defines the baseline permissions for API access, and reporting. Core Configuration Bundle: Installs the core metadata, system configurations, and sample profiles. Ideal for users starting with a clean slate but wanting to handle layouts manually. Enhanced Experience Bundle: Installs FlexiPages, page layouts, and lightweight sample data for immediate visualization.

findings.name: Core Configuration Bundle Specifications
findings.detail: This bundle installs the building blocks of Customer Engagement, focusing on administrative and system-level settings. Core Metadata for System Administrator: Configures the settings related to these features: Activity Plan, Provider Affiliation, Best Time, External Search, Insights, Inventory Management, Key Account Management, Next Best Customer, Consent, Planner, Search Before Create, Licenses, Territory Management, Territory User Downtime, and Video Call. Business Operations Data: Deploys the configuration data stored in objects that control application-wide behavior for provider visit settings, account dynamic list configuration, account filter config, account list actions, account search preferences, presentation settings, email settings, sample inventory management profile settings, external search settings, and sample limit settings. Foundation Profile: Includes the LSC Custom Profile, which defines the baseline permissions for API access and reporting. Offline Framework: Automates the deployment of object metadata cache configurations, ensuring the features are prepared for offline data synchronization.

findings.name: Enhanced Experience Bundle Specifications
findings.detail: This bundle deploys the front-end interface and the records necessary to demonstrate the application's functional workflows. It combines comprehensive metadata with seed data to provide a fully realized environment. Lightning Interface: Installs a comprehensive set of FlexiPages, page layouts, and action overrides, including specialized layouts for healthcare professionals (HCP), healthcare organizations (HCO), and contact point addresses. Object Configuration: Deploys objects with compact layouts, field sets, and record types, along with standard value sets for picklist fields, to ensure data consistency. Access & Permissions: Includes profiles pre-configured with field permissions, layout assignments, record type visibilities, and tab visibilities. Pre-Configured Home Page: Activates the Home Page LSC Default, featuring integrated widgets for Announcements, Next Best Customer recommendations, and Activity Plan tracking. Functional Seed Data: Populates the environment with a representative dataset, including sample HCP Accounts, Visit records, Account Plans, and Medical Inquiries.

findings.name: Visualize Success with Sample Data
findings.detail: During setup, you are prompted to include sample data, which populates your org with realistic records to help your teams explore the Customer Engagement capabilities immediately after installation. HCP Accounts: Includes a pre-configured HCP account linked to products and territories. Engagement Tools: Pre-populated visits and calendar entries. KAM Objectives: sample account plans and objectives for key account managers. Medical Inquiries: A mix of open and resolved inquiries to demonstrate the workflow.

findings.name: Post-Setup Tasks
findings.detail: After completing either the standard installation or Enhanced Experience bundle of the custom installation, perform these tasks to ensure that the core Customer Engagement features are ready for testing. Activate the LSC Territory Model territory model. For instructions, see Activate a Territory Model . Assign the System Administrator to the TM - SPC - San Francisco North 20D02T11 territory. For instructions, see Assign Users to Territories . Share the required data with territories. Run Medical Inquiry Sharing Job . Run Visit Share Management Jobs . Product Alignment Jobs Ensure that the active territory in Territory Switcher is TM - SPC - San Francisco North 20D02T11. Add the All Account Plans list view to the Account Plans tab.

findings.name: Set Up the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile App
findings.detail: Set up the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app to enable your field users to securely connect with healthcare professionals and organizations through their iPads. Field users can access and work with critical data, content (PDFs, HTML5, videos), reports, and smart summaries with or without an internet connection.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app is available for iPad in the Apple App Store . Supported devices: iPad, iPad Air, and iPad Pro models that Apple introduced on or after January 1, 2024. Support includes Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi + Cellular variants, all supported screen sizes, and all factory storage configurations. Eligibility is based on the model introduction date, not the purchase date. iPad mini isn't supported. Supported OS Versions: iOS 26.0+ Note Flows are not supported in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Customize the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile App Help your field teams manage their daily tasks efficiently using the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. Configure object metadata cache settings, application settings, profile-based configurations, and UI customizations to control data access, feature behavior, and the overall mobile app experience for your organization. Synchronization Management Define device synchronization settings between the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app and your Salesforce org to support data management and control. Help your mobile app users keep their data current so they can make well-informed decisions. Deep Linking for the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile App Your sales reps rely on their mobile devices to perform complex tasks and navigate between multiple tabs, records, or actions. With deep linking, you can use supported URL schemes to send users directly to the right spot in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app from a third-party or web app. For example, deep links can open specific records, create a record with prepopulated data, or perform a specific action when the app opens. Life Sciences Cloud (LSC) Apps LSC Apps are custom Lightning web components (LWCs) that you can create and embed on the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. These apps help you to design and implement complex features and integrations on Lightning pages and in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Mobile Device Management with the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile App The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports Mobile Device Management (MDM) through the Salesforce Mobile SDK's managed app configuration. When you manage the app with MDM, field users don't download or update the app from the public Apple App Store. Instead, you control whether field users get the app and its updates from your enterprise app store or whether the MDM provider delivers updates directly to their devices. Global Search in the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile App Quickly find information in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app by using the Global Search feature to search across a predefined set of objects and fields within the iPad database. You can instantly access recently viewed records via Global Search. findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. LWC quick actions run as web components embedded in the app and communicate directly with the Salesforce server, much like using Salesforce in a browser. When offline mode is off, data saved through an LWC quick action doesn't pass through the app's local database, so the app isn't aware of the change until the next sync pulls it down from the server. When offline mode is on, LWC components can resolve requests from the local database. See LSC Apps Offline Support . The type of Lightning web component (LWC) change determines whether to regenerate the metadata cache: New LWC: When you add a new LWC to a Lightning page or configure it as a quick action, regenerate the metadata cache. The mobile app downloads the updated metadata to recognize the new component. Customize and Send Emails Send emails to healthcare professionals (HCPs) and healthcare organizations (HCOs) from any point in your workflow. Present Content to Your Customers Present slides, PDFs, embedded videos, and dynamic content to enhance your interactions with healthcare professionals (HCPs). findings.name: Version 262.15.1.0
findings.detail: This patch contains fixes to ensure that the Life Sciences Clouds for Customer Engagement features work correctly. Feature | Issue | Description Inventory Management | Selecting a discrepancy reason for a zero-stock inventory count triggered a false validation error, preventing field reps from submitting the assessment. | Validation rules now allow successful submission of zero-quantity inventory counts so field reps can complete month-end reconciliation and report depleted stock. Field reps couldn't submit inventory counts for shared product lots if another rep had an unresolved over-disbursement on the same lot. | The submission process now checks only for the active user’s disbursements, allowing field reps to submit inventory counts for shared product lots.

findings.name: Version 262.15.0.0
findings.detail: This patch contains fixes to ensure that the Life Sciences Clouds for Customer Engagement features work correctly. Feature | Issue | Description Consent Management | Users without an authorized consent-management role could update participant consent records on events, such as marking invitations or attendance as paper-signed, leading to inaccurate regulated consent information. | The consent upload process now verifies user authorization before processing updates, ensuring only authorized users can change participant consent statuses. General | Filter and sort inputs used when selecting object were not properly validated, which could allow a user to retrieve records beyond their permitted visibility. | Filter and sort inputs are now validated, so users can retrieve only the records they are permitted to access. Intelligent Content | Users without the required administrative permission could initiate email-fragment sharing across information beyond their normal access. | Email fragment sharing now enforces the required permission, so only authorized users can start the process. The content stored in a presentation or email template could run in another authenticated user's browser when the content was opened in the web email template editor. This could expose information or allow unauthorized actions and content changes. | The email template editor now handles records securely to prevent stored values from running unauthorized browser actions. Key Account Management | Users without the required permissions could create assessment tasks and action plan items for account plans, potentially adding unauthorized or inaccurate planning information. | Saving assessment tasks and action plan items now checks user permissions, so records are created only for users with the appropriate access. Remote Engagement | During a remote engagement session, enabling the field rep's camera while sharing content resized the shared content and cropped part of it. This could prevent attendees from seeing the complete approved, safety, or regulatory content. | The shared-content layout now stays intact when the rep turns their camera on or off during screen sharing, keeping the full content visible throughout the session. When a guest enabled their camera while a field rep was sharing content, the attendee's video took over the full screen and hid the shared content. | The session layout is now corrected so that shared content remains in the main viewing area and the guest's camera appears in a smaller video tile without interrupting the presentation. Visit Management | In a remote Twilio visit, requesting a signature for the parent visit after adding samples and DTP displayed a validation error. | Signature validation is now corrected so that users can request a signature for the parent visit without an error. Completing a remote Twilio visit with products and an approved signature created disbursement and requested-sample records, but failed to deduct or update sample limits. | Remote Twilio visits now create the sample limit transaction records and correctly deduct sample limits when a visit is submitted after a product signature is approved. Field reps could not open the switch account list in the visit engagement flow. It returned an internal server error and no accounts loaded, which prevented these reps from logging visits. | Field reps can open switch account, view the accounts and healthcare providers aligned to their territories, and continue logging the visit.

findings.name: Version 262.13.0.0
findings.detail: This patch contains fixes to ensure that the Life Sciences Clouds for Customer Engagement features work correctly. Feature | Issue | Description Account Management | Data Change Requests couldn't be created or approved when profile-based creation was disabled, updates used system mode, or the user's country configurations differed from record types. | Data Change Request processing now supports creation with the profile setting disabled, approval of updated records in system mode, and creation across mismatched country and record-type settings. Event Management | Field reps received an access-denied error when attempting to launch a group Visit from an approved Managed Event. | The required group-Visit controller is now included in the Life Sciences core permission set, giving eligible field reps access to the launch group visit. General | Administrative setting labels in the mobile app, such as Metadata Cache and Object settings, were displayed in English regardless of the user's configured language. | Headings, fields, filters, operators, actions, placeholders, and notifications on administration screens can now be translated. Intelligent Content | Users couldn't move forward or backward within videos in multichannel presentations, even though the same videos worked correctly on an iPad. | The presentation player now responds to the video progress control, so users can move forward or backward within videos. The Intelligent Content presentation player displayed the email action twice. | The presentation player now displays the email action just once. Sending or canceling an email from a visit redirected users to an invalid URL. | The email wizard now decodes the encoded return path before building the redirect URL, returning users to the Visit detail page. The Send Email consent flow prompted users to draw a signature even though signature capture was not supported, resulting in consent records that did not retain the signature. | The consent flow no longer displays the unsupported signature option, preventing users from providing a signature that cannot be saved. Presentations created in Intelligent Content on an iPad did not appear in My Presentations on the Desktop site after synchronization. | My Presentations on the desktop site now displays presentations created and synchronized from the mobile app. The email batch process continued retrying failed emails beyond the configured limit and sent emails through the substitute-address workflow even when records were no longer marked to be sent. | Failed emails are now excluded from further retry and send attempts once they reach the configured retry limit. Inventory Management | The Description field on the Create Product Request and View Product Request Create pages used different labels. | The Product Request pages now use the same label for the Description field. Visit Management | Users could clear a required number field while editing a visit and save the record without receiving a required-field error. | Required number fields are now validated when users edit a visit, preventing them from saving until they enter a value. Submitting an edited visit deleted assessment tasks created outside the visit workspace because those tasks were omitted from the visit submission data. | Visit submission now preserves Assessment Tasks created outside the visit workspace while continuing to process task changes made within the visit workflow. The Visit Engagement page loaded slowly and inconsistently when opened for the first time due to delays in retrieving label resources. | Label resources now load more efficiently, reducing initial loading delays on the Visit Engagement page. Remote Engagement | During a remote engagement, a consent signature prompt briefly appeared at the top of the page or remained displayed after the request was canceled. | Consent signature prompts now open and close within the consent panel without appearing elsewhere on the remote engagement page. During a remote engagement, hosts lost access to the presentation controls after turning on their camera. | Presentation controls now remain visible and available while the host's camera is turned on. During a remote engagement, a participant's camera feed could disappear when the host turned on their camera, and the host lost access to camera visibility controls. | Participant camera feeds now remain visible when the host turns on their camera, and hosts maintain access to the camera-feed visibility control. During remote engagements, participant video disappeared after the host enabled their camera, presentation menu buttons stopped responding, and the right navigation arrow disappeared upon resizing the window. | Participant video now remains visible, presentation menu controls stay responsive when the host's camera is on, and slide navigation arrows remain available at supported window sizes. When a host requested a signature while sharing a presentation, participants could see the host's signature request form or action menu. | Signature request forms and related host controls are no longer visible to participants when a presentation is shared. When on-device HCP consent was enabled, a consent signature request sent to a mobile participant expired immediately and hosts received an error notification with no explanation. | Mobile participants can now complete consent signature requests when on-device HCP consent is enabled, and hosts receive a clear notification if an error occurs. After a host rejected a signature and requested another, the Approve option appeared too soon and opened an empty signature window. | Signature updates now apply only to the current request, so a rejected request cannot change the status of a signature request. Remote engagement failed to start because the conference launcher could not access the call identifier required by the host component. | The host component's call identifier is now accessible to the conference launcher, allowing the remote engagement to start.

findings.name: Version 262.12.0.0
findings.detail: This patch contains fixes to ensure that the Life Sciences Clouds for Customer Engagement features work correctly. Feature | Issue | Description Account Search | Record type-specific picklist values were not enforced on ContactPointAddress fields during SBC Account creation, allowing restricted picklist options to appear on the Account Creation screen. | Updated the account creation flow to enforce record type-specific picklist restrictions so users only see and select valid picklist values. Labels on the Account Additional Information tab and account registration menu appeared in English regardless of localized settings. | Added full localization support to Account Additional Information tab and account registration menu labels. Activity Timeline | Changes to Activity Timeline Visibility Settings (in the Admin Console) for the Visit object were not saved when selecting a field set. | Fixed configuration persistence logic in the Admin Console to properly save Activity Timeline field set settings for the Visit object. Event Management | Updating event participant records triggered unnecessary quota recalculation queries even when quota-related fields were unchanged, degrading system performance. | Added field-change guards so quota recalculations run only when relevant fields, such as Response Status or Attributed To, are updated. Saving a large number of attendees on a Managed Event experienced delays due to small transaction chunk sizes. | Increased the batch processing chunk size for attendee updates on Managed Events, significantly reducing save times while remaining within platform governor limits. Pagination requests in the Update Attendees screen transferred redundant record ID data, slowing screen performance. | Optimized pagination request payloads in the Update Attendees window by removing redundant record references, improving screen responsiveness. Selecting accounts in the Update Attendees window caused the web UI to freeze temporarily in territories with large account datasets. | Improved front-end component performance in the Update Attendees window to ensure instant checkbox selection without UI responsiveness issues. The Estimated Expense Allocation screen filtered available participants using actual expense rules rather than estimated expense configurations. | Updated participant filtering logic in the Estimated Expense Allocation screen to correctly apply estimated expense configuration rules. General | Navigating to Account Team Member records from the related list caused a JavaScript error when handling toast notifications that were missing expected parameters. | Added null guards and parameter validation to toast notification handlers in generic related lists to ensure smooth navigation. Home Page | On desktop site, the Up Next (Upcoming Agenda) home page component incorrectly listed completed visits alongside planned visits. | Updated component filtering to exclude completed visits, ensuring only planned upcoming visits appear across desktop and mobile platforms. Intelligent Content | Unsupported PDF presentations appeared as selectable options in the New Custom Presentation creation window. | Updated the custom presentation creation window to filter out PDF presentations, ensuring only supported presentation formats are displayed. Certain email UI elements, including help links, picklist values, status values, and call-to-action buttons, were displayed in English regardless of localized language settings. | Updated UI labels, status values, and action buttons across email features to appropriately support multi-language localization. Filter labels and UI elements on the Intelligent Content Filter screen were displayed in English regardless of language settings. | Localized all UI text and filter labels on the Intelligent Content Filter screen to align with the user's selected language. License Management | The "Modify Formulas on Business License Object" log label in License Management was hardcoded in English. | Added localization support for log labels in License Management to align with the user's language settings. Lists and Filters | Saving a newly created, empty Account Filter failed with a ListException error when adding the initial field via "Select Fields to Display." | Resolved field creation handling logic for empty filters so initial field additions save successfully. Remote Engagement | A malformed participant identity in a video consultation room could cause participant connection failures for health care providers and field representatives. | Added server-side validation and error handling for participant identities during video room connections to ensure stable, reliable consultation sessions. The Consent Details window displayed Contact Point names instead of Engagement Channel Type names. | Updated the Consent Details window to display Engagement Channel Type names, providing clear visibility into communication channels associated with consent records. Rescheduling a virtual visit sent reschedule email notifications containing incorrect meeting IDs to attendees, impacting participant joining and attendance tracking. | Updated reschedule email notification logic to send each attendee their unique and correct meeting ID. Sales Data | Scrolling the Measure Total Summary table on the Sales chart component caused a null pointer error and disrupted chart rendering. | Fixed scroll event handling in the Measure summary table to prevent null object errors and maintain continuous chart visibility. Sample Limits | Assigning templates to products failed with an Apex heap size limit error in orgs with large product catalogs. | Optimized the product hierarchy query and rendering logic to stay within governor limits, allowing successful template assignments regardless of product catalog size. Visit Management | Creating a visit with specific products failed with a SOQL governor limit error when sample limit validation was enabled in Admin Console. | Optimized sample limits validation queries during visit creation to eliminate governor limit errors and ensure smooth visit creation.

findings.name: Version 262.10.0.0
findings.detail: This patch contains fixes to ensure that the Life Sciences Clouds for Customer Engagement features work correctly. Feature | Issue | Description Data Change Requests | When creating accounts with associated addresses, affiliations, or specialties, child Data Change Requests (DCRs) were generated without linking to their parent DCR, breaking parent-child DCR relationships. | Resolved a mapping failure during record creation to ensure parent DCR IDs are propagated to all child DCRs across both Desktop site and Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. Data Change Requests (DCR) for Healthcare Provider Specialty records failed to trigger when specific managed fields were updated, despite deploying recommended package updates. | Resolved the nested trigger conflict where the DCR validity state was incorrectly shared across objects. Scoped the validity state evaluation per SObjectType to prevent cross-trigger interference and ensure DCRs trigger as expected.

findings.name: Version 262.9.0.0
findings.detail: This patch contains fixes to ensure that the Life Sciences Clouds for Customer Engagement features work correctly. Feature | Issue | Description Activity Timeline | Visits weren’t appearing on the Activity Timeline tab of Account records, preventing users from seeing full account engagement history. | Corrected the activity query and filtering logic for Account Activity Timelines. All visit activities now properly render in the timeline display. Event Management | When adding actual or estimated expenses to a managed event, the Expense Type dropdown incorrectly showed options meant only for visits. | Updated the filtering logic for Managed Event expense types so that only options designated for Managed Event are shown. Users were unable to allocate Managed Event expenses to write-in or non-profiled attendees because those attendee types were missing from the Allocate Expense window. | Non-profiled and write-in attendees are now correctly shown in the Allocate Expense window based on event settings. Updating the Invitation-Sent status for an event organizer failed when attendees were present on the event. | Fixed the database query responsible for generating territory sharing records, allowing organizer invitation statuses to be updated when attendees are attached. The MonetaryCapsRecalculationJob batch job failed due to Apex CPU time limit timeouts caused by redundant sorting of incoming records. | Removed the background sorting step, optimizing CPU performance, and allowing the batch calculations to finish without timing out. General | Date and time fields appeared in an incorrect format within the LSCGenericRelatedList Aura component. | Corrected the custom implementation to ensure the date and time appear accurately across the LSCGenericRelatedList component. Access Check Failed error pop-ups appeared repeatedly when accessing or managing configurations on the Trigger Handlers page in the Admin Console. | Added the missing orderByField and sortingOrder attribute declarations to the component and updated access-check handling. This change prevents internal server errors (GACKs) and allows admins to sort and manage trigger handlers. Guest Users | Guest users were unable to complete self-registration on Experience Cloud sites sandboxes due to system permission errors when accessing restricted object types. | Updated the underlying package classes to resolve references to restricted objects dynamically. This change prevents class-load failures during unauthenticated sessions and restores guest self-registration functionality. Intelligent Content | Text elements in the Intelligent Content admin console and presentation views didn’t support language translations. | Replaced all hardcoded text strings with custom labels to support localization, translation, and consistent UI messaging across all Intelligent Content workflows. When Drawing mode was enabled during a presentation, the Menu Player trigger icon disappeared from the page, preventing users from reopening the navigation menu. | Updated the presentation player layout so the Menu Player trigger icon remains visible and functional when Drawing mode is active. Hyperlinks embedded within PDFs weren’t clickable in Intelligent Content. | All embedded links in Intelligent Content are now fully interactive and clickable. Sample Limits | When running batch jobs to assign multiple cloned templates for the same product to an account, the existing Product and Service Lifecycle (PSL) records were incorrectly updated instead of creating records. | Updated the batch assignment processing logic to make sure that assigning multiple cloned templates for the same product generates new PSL records as intended, preventing existing records from being overwritten. Visit Engagement | The General section header in Pre-Provider Visit Notes was missing from the Visit Engagement window on the desktop site, despite appearing correctly in the mobile app. | Updated the desktop Visit Engagement component to make sure that General header and its translations render correctly on the desktop site.

In the Account Picker component, a query limit error occurred when attempting to fetch only accounts associated with an HCP. | The query logic has been optimized to prevent limit errors when fetching associated accounts. An error occurred when a boolean field was configured as a Provider Account Territory Info searchable field in the Account Search Preference settings. | Account search preferences now correctly handle all data types, allowing boolean fields to be used as searchable fields without error. Object Metadata Cache Configuration | The validation status of the Object Metadata Cache Configuration records isn’t accurately shown. | The validation status is now correctly reflecting. Calendar | Available visits weren't shown in Calendar even when filters are set to show all visits. | The display logic is corrected to ensure that all available visits are now properly shown according to the applied filter settings. Ratings | PrvdAccountUserGroupInfo entity were not visible in the Ratings layout. | The Ratings layout now correctly shows all the PrvdAccountUserGroupInfo fields. Sample Limits | Users encountered an error (gack) when trying to view or save sample limit templates in the Admin Console. | Fixed the issue that caused users to see an error (gack).
